newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares rose in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares rose in quiet trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose on Tuesday in quiet trade with clear uptrends, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index was 0.99 points up to close at 240.76 points in turnover of 23.7 million pounds ($6.97 million).
The sectors of cements and millers were the market dominants.
"They are the traditional favrourites, in additional to the housing and banking sectors," Vice President of Hermes Financial, Ahmed el-Helw, told Reuters.
Suez Cement, the most active stock, rose 0.55 pounds to end at 49.10.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills, the second most active, also finished 0.20 pounds up to 49.20.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development jumped 10.00 pounds to end at 188.00 pounds.
"The share was undervalued recently," Helw said. "Moreover, they are going to distribute a dividend of 10 pounds per share soon."
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 360.89 points from 358.00 on Monday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 169.65 from 169.32 points.
